text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- Serbian parliament panel discussion on the local elections and role of the media holds first session and determines rules of procedure. Opposition deputies not participating.
- U.N. extends mandate of observers in the Prevlaka promontory to July 15.
- Visiting Italian envoy Piero Fassino says the outcome of the Yugoslav crisis is in sight.
- Yugoslavia should seek the status of a developing country in the World Trade Organisation, federal government commission says.

- Yugoslav steel industry produced 568,500 tonnes of iron in 1996 as against 525,500 tonnes in 1991 reaching its pre-sanction production level, says Arsenije Jovanovic president of the Yugoslav black metallurgy association.
- Prices of three staples -- oil, milk and flour go up.
- Reasons for the fluctuation of the dinar black market exchange rate are non-economic and psychological, says Dragan Tomic minister coordinator in the Serbian government.

- The Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) main board excludes from the party Belgrade mayor Nebojisa Covic and (former head of Nis socialists) Mile Ilic and replaces head of Belgrade socialists Branislav Ivkovic appointing Serbian Palriament Sepaker Dragan Tomic as acting chairman.
- Belgrade municipal election commission reinstates local election results from November 17 giving opposition Zajedno the majority of 60 seats in the 110-seat municipal council.
- The Nis electoral commission also recognises majority of 41 seats for opposiiton coalition Zajedno in the 7-seat city council.
- The Belgrade university council is to hold a session Wednesday morning to discuss normalisation of classes and to hold a no-confidence vote to rector Dragutin Velickovic.
- Serbia's postal company PTT signs 80-million German mark deal with Siemens of Germany.
- Representatives of Italian invstment construction firms Studio Legale Finanziario Valutario from Bologna and Torno from Milan visit Yugoslavia to determine investment possibilities.
NASA BORBA
- Opposition cautious about decisions of the Belgrade and Nis electoral commissions to acknowledge coalition Zajedno victory at November 17 local elections.

- The Italian government insists on recognition of November 17 election results and dialogue with democratic opposition in Serbia, says envoy Piero Fassino after talks with opposition leader Vuk Draskovic and student protest representatives.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- Radio Television Serbia does not believe the takeover of some city councils by the opposition will affect its editorial policy as it is under authority of the republic although it expects to have competition in the local media.
- Yugoslav and Croatian commissions for missing persons hold session in Belgrade.
